name: Sassafras Beer
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: large handful of dried apples
ingredients.originalText: a large handful of dried apples

ingredients.name: strong fresh yeast
ingredients.originalText: half a pint of strong fresh yeast

ingredients.name: piece of sassafras root the size of an egg
ingredients.originalText: a piece of sassafras root the size of an egg

instructions.text: Put all the ingredients (except the molasses and yeast) at once into a large kettle
Boil it till the apples are quite soft
Put the molasses into a small clean tub or a large pan
Set a hair sieve over the vessel, and strain the mixture through it
Let it stand till it becomes only milkwarm, and then stir in the yeast
Put the liquor immediately into the keg or jugs, and let it stand uncorked to ferment
Fill the jugs quite full, that the liquor in fermenting may run over
Set them in a large tub
When you see that the fermentation or working has subsided, cork it, and it will be fit for use next day

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put all the ingredients (except the molasses and yeast) at once into a large kettle
2. Boil it till the apples are quite soft
3. Put the molasses into a small clean tub or a large pan
4. Set a hair sieve over the vessel, and strain the mixture through it
5. Let it stand till it becomes only milkwarm, and then stir in the yeast
6. Put the liquor immediately into the keg or jugs, and let it stand uncorked to ferment
7. Fill the jugs quite full, that the liquor in fermenting may run over
8. Set them in a large tub
9. When you see that the fermentation or working has subsided, cork it, and it will be fit for use next day
